# everpure_azure_volume (Resource)

Manages a Volume on a Volume Group.

~> **Destroying the parent volume group soft-deletes this volume with it.** The backend destroys every volume in a volume group as part of destroying the group itself; all of it stays recoverable until eradication. See [Deletion policies](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/guides/deletion-policies).

To read a volume managed elsewhere without taking ownership of it, use the [`everpure_azure_volume` data source](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/data-sources/volume).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "storage_pool_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Full ARM ID of an existing Everpure Storage Pool in the same subscription."
}

resource "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  name            = "vg-prod-east"
  storage_pool_id = var.storage_pool_id
}

resource "everpure_azure_volume" "example" {
  name            = "vol-prod-data"
  volume_group_id = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id

  # Can be increased in place; decreasing is rejected.
  provisioned_size_in_gib = 100

  # provisioned_size_in_bytes exists for sizes that are not a whole GiB.
}

# A volume cloned from an existing one. source_volume_id and
# source_type are create-only: changing either forces a new volume to be
# created. The clone inherits its source's size, so no size attribute is set
# here.
resource "everpure_azure_volume" "clone" {
  name             = "vol-prod-data-clone"
  volume_group_id  = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  source_type      = "volume"
  source_volume_id = everpure_azure_volume.example.id

  # Overrides the defaults, which normally protect a volume from destroy.
  deletion_protection  = false # true (default) blocks destroy + replace
  eradicate_on_destroy = true  # false (default) soft-deletes, recoverable
}

# A volume recovered after it was soft-deleted. The source must be in the same
# volume group, and is addressed by the timestamped name soft deletion gave it.
# Recovering restores that volume under the name given here; it does not copy it.
resource "everpure_azure_volume" "restored_soft_deleted" {
  name                         = "vol-prod-data-restored-soft-deleted"
  volume_group_id              = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  source_type                  = "recoverableVolume"
  source_recoverable_volume_id = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east/volumeGroups/vg-prod-east/volumes/vol-prod-data-20260827141136"
}

# A volume restored from a volume group snapshot. Like the clone above, the
# restored volume inherits its source's size. volume_name is the name the
# source volume had when the snapshot was taken.
resource "everpure_azure_volume" "restored" {
  name            = "vol-prod-data-restored"
  volume_group_id = everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  source_type     = "snapshot"

  source_snapshot {
    id          = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east/volumeGroups/vg-prod-east/snapshots/snap-2026-09-01"
    volume_name = "vol-prod-data"
  }
}

output "volume_id" {
  value = everpure_azure_volume.example.id
}

output "volume_serial_number" {
  value = everpure_azure_volume.example.serial_number
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the volume. The name must be 2-40 characters, start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, numbers and hyphens. Changing this forces a new volume to be created.
- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group this volume lives on. Changing this forces a new volume to be created.

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether to block destroying this volume, or replacing it (which destroys it as part of the replacement). Defaults to `true`. Set to `false`, and apply, before a destroy or a change that would otherwise force replacement.
- `eradicate_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether destroy permanently eradicates the volume instead of soft-deleting it. Defaults to `false`. There is no recovery window once eradicated.
- `provisioned_size_in_bytes` (Number) Provisioned size of the volume, in bytes. Must be at least 1048576 (1 MiB) and a multiple of 512. The canonical size attribute: it is always populated, including when the volume's size comes from `provisioned_size_in_gib` or from a source that isn't a whole number of gibibytes. Conflicts with `provisioned_size_in_gib`. Can be changed in place, but to a larger value only.
- `provisioned_size_in_gib` (Number) Provisioned size of the volume, in gibibytes (GiB, 1024^3 bytes). A shorthand for `provisioned_size_in_bytes` that saves writing the size out in bytes, and the preferred way to set the size when it is a whole number of gibibytes. Conflicts with `provisioned_size_in_bytes`. Can be changed in place, to a larger value only.
- `source_recoverable_volume_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the soft-deleted volume to recover — a soft-deleted volume keeps its own, renamed volume resource path, so this has the same shape as `source_volume_id`. Required when `source_type` is `recoverableVolume`, and must be unset otherwise. Must be in the same volume group as `volume_group_id`. Changing this forces a new volume to be created.
- `source_serial_number` (String) Serial number of the volume to clone from, for cloning a volume that was created through Platform Console rather than through Azure. The source volume is left unchanged. Required when `source_type` is `serialNumber`, and must be unset otherwise. The source must be in the same storage pool as `volume_group_id`, and cannot be a volume managed through Azure; use `source_volume_id` to clone those. Changing this forces a new volume to be created.
- `source_snapshot` (Block List) The volume group snapshot and member volume to restore from. Required when `source_type` is `snapshot`, and must be absent otherwise. Create-only: changing, adding or removing this block forces a new volume to be created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--source_snapshot))
- `source_type` (String) How the volume's initial contents are created. One of `none` (empty, the default, sized from `provisioned_size_in_bytes`/`provisioned_size_in_gib`), `volume` (clone from `source_volume_id`), `serialNumber` (clone from `source_serial_number`), `snapshot` (restore from `source_snapshot`), or `recoverableVolume` (recover from `source_recoverable_volume_id`). An imported volume always shows `none` here, since the API cannot report a volume's origin after the fact. Changing this forces a new volume to be created.
- `source_volume_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume to clone from. Required when `source_type` is `volume`, and must be unset otherwise. Must be in the same storage pool as `volume_group_id`. Changing this forces a new volume to be created.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume, e.g. `/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool1/volumeGroups/vg1/volumes/vol1`.
- `serial_number` (String) The volume's own serial number. Visible in the VM as the disk/drive serial number. Unique for each volume, so can be used to distinguish volumes with identical sizes. It cannot be used as another volume's `source_serial_number`: cloning by serial number applies only to volumes created directly on the storage pool, for those created through Azure use `source_volume_id`.

<a id="nestedblock--source_snapshot"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source_snapshot`

Required:

- `id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group snapshot containing the volume snapshot to restore. Must be in the same storage pool as `volume_group_id`.
- `volume_name` (String) Name of the member volume, within the volume group snapshot named by `id`, to restore — i.e. the source volume's own name at the time the snapshot was taken.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Defaults to 20 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when creating the volume.
- `delete` (String) Defaults to 35 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when destroying the volume, including eradicating its recoverable copy when eradicate_on_destroy is set.
- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the volume.
- `update` (String) Defaults to 20 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when updating the volume.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = everpure_azure_volume.example
  identity = {
    subscription_id     = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
    storage_pool_name   = "pool-prod-east"
    volume_group_name   = "vg-prod-east"
    name                = "vol-prod-data"
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_volume" "example" {
  # ... configuration matching the imported volume
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the volume.
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the resource lives in.
- `storage_pool_name` (String) Name of the storage pool the volume belongs to.
- `subscription_id` (String) Azure subscription ID the resource lives in.
- `volume_group_name` (String) Name of the volume group the volume belongs to.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Volumes are imported by their full Azure resource ID.
terraform import everpure_azure_volume.example \
  "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east/volumeGroups/vg-prod-east/volumes/vol-prod-data"
```
